what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours, 9 commits, two substantive, and the honest summary is that this stretch built instruments and measured nothing. First correct the brief again, for the fifth consecutive stretch: it reports `previous_focus_drawn.drawn: []`. All four items were worked -- `3cefa754b` landed the noise-floor arm as a committed mode with mutation-proven tests, `9e52d2254` landed the pounds-based household decision and narrowed the elasticity spread, `4b6e1b29f` closed EP1 with a corrected diagnosis, `e0cce68d1` relaunched the A/B reparented. The steer is biting; the control keys on maturity-map atom ids and cannot see a Lane 0 slug. Now the substance. The value-cycle case still rests entirely on readings taken in the NARROW world -- `level_share_of_advantage` 119.7%, `selection_gbp` -£1,388.80 over the decade -- and the widened world that was supposed to test them has now failed to be measured twice in one day: killed 4m28s in at 15:08Z, then gate-refused at 19:55:59Z when the reparented unit's land phase hit two red tests and correctly declined to measure an unlanded world. The unit reads `failed`; `value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json` does not exist; `simulation/customer_events.py` and `simulation/run_phase2b.py` are still dirty. The `--noise-floor-seeds` mode was built and never run, so the -£1,388.80 still has no error bar. Against the thesis that is not nothing -- a BASELINE exists and it is currently BEATING the per-customer arm, which is the most important and least flattering thing this project has established -- but we cannot yet say whether that finding survives a world with anything in it to select on, and that is now the whole question. On the company side the stretch produced the one genuinely good result: the third reading of EP1 found the real cause of the constant hazard and it is the HARNESS, not the company. The coupler grades every account at its first year-end, where `churn_probability = BASE + 0 x UPLIFT` because no bill-shock history has accrued, so `distinct_hazards: 1` was a property of the selection rule and never evidence that the estimator cannot tell accounts apart -- it discriminates fine, 100 of 101 multi-snapshot accounts move off their first value. EP1 sits at level 2 with "has not been graded ONCE" written in its own map entry. Net: not backwards, but the imbalance my predecessor named -- widening the world is cheaper than measuring it -- is wider tonight than it was this afternoon, and every item below exists to close it.

focus.what: Fix the coupler's belief-selection rule so EP1 grades a belief that is capable of varying. Observed and written up in `docs/observability/EP1_GRADED_SLICE_WHAT_IT_IS_EVIDENCE_FOR_2026-08-27.md`: `tools/couple_clv.py`'s `_earliest_belief` takes each account's FIRST year-end snapshot, which is exactly the point where `churn_probability = BASE + 0 x UPLIFT` (`saas/churn_model.py:39`, `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py:580`) because no bill-shock history has accrued yet -- so the hazard is 0.05 for 154 of 154 accounts by construction, and `distinct_hazards: 1` measures the rule, not the company. The stated justification for taking the earliest snapshot -- that a ceased account has no other -- is false for 14 of the 20 graded accounts still present. Replace it with a rule that grades a belief the company actually held while the account was live, state the rule and its reason in the module docstring beside the one it replaces, and keep the existing fallback for accounts that genuinely have one snapshot. R15 both ways: the mutation that must go red is reverting to the earliest snapshot and asserting `distinct_hazards` stays above one; and the new rule must not pass by reading a field the belief producer also writes -- trace which field, per this project's own catalogued lesson that a cross-layer import is not automatically a tautology. Then run `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and land the row. The headline `gap = 2.529` stays UNPUBLISHED until the row is honest.
focus.why: This is the company half of the thesis and the only instrument that grades whether the supplier's per-customer lifetime-value belief is worth anything -- and it is currently structurally incapable of telling us. The atom's own map entry says it plainly: level 2, "EP1 has not been graded ONCE". It is ranked third rather than last on purpose, for the second stretch running: it sat last on six lists and was reached on none of them, it moved up last time and was reached, and it is independent of the tree lock so it can proceed while item two's run is in flight. Finished when the ledger row is measured under the new rule and states how many distinct hazards the graded population now contains. If that is more than one and the coupled rung is met, a level move is available on that evidence -- self-certify with `record_level_up_self_certified`, and never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change. R12: the gap is a diagnostic and never a thing to move. If the belief turns out to be badly calibrated once it can vary, that is a finding and not a defect in the fix.

focus.what: The control the director asked for landed in `9e52d2254` and covers three of the five axes that make the claim, so the class is not closed. Observed: `tests/simulation/test_discoverability_claims_are_enforced.py::_axes()` filters on `key.endswith("_marginals")`, which admits `green_stance`, `price_sensitivity` and `channel_pref` and silently drops two keys in the same file that also carry the flag -- `tenure_adoption_gating_strength` and `region_marginal_synthetic_acquisitions`. BOTH declare `hidden_truth_only: false`, i.e. both claim to be discoverable, and neither has a probe. Tenure is the sharp one: its own note reads "the company must DISCOVER that tenure gates adoption from its acquisition/interaction data (the coupled-triad gap)" -- a discovery route asserted in the curriculum that no test demonstrates exists. Compounding it, the whole-set guard `MIN_AXES_SCANNED = 3` is pinned to whatever the suffix filter happens to return, so the one control meant to catch a missed axis cannot see the axes the filter drops. Widen `_axes()` to every key carrying `hidden_truth_only` regardless of name, re-base the floor on the widened scan, and then for each newly covered axis either wire a probe from the DECISION's side (the way `_probe_price_sensitivity` does -- never by importing the function you are trying to prove is called) or mark it hidden with the reason recorded. R15: the mutation that must go red is adding a sixth flagged key, named without the `_marginals` suffix, carrying a fabricated channel note.
focus.why: R10 -- an absurdity-class defect does not close with an instance fix, and this one closed with an instance fix wearing a class's clothes. The director's words at 16:36Z were "if a trait has no channel the company can observe, either give it one or mark it hidden. Don't leave it claiming discoverable and don't wait for me to say so", and two traits still do. It matters to the thesis directly and not as tidying: the thesis says the advantage must come from INFERENCE and never ACCESS, and the mirror of that is that a declared inference route must be real -- a company that tried to learn tenure from its interaction data would be right to try, would fail forever, and we would read that as a poor model rather than an impossible task. Fourth because it is a control and nothing above it waits on it. Finished when the scan enumerates every declared axis rather than every axis with a particular suffix, the floor cannot be satisfied by the filter's own blindness, and each of the two newly visible axes either has a probe or is marked hidden with its reason on the record.

The third and final reading of EP1's constant hazard, correcting two previous directions including mine. Direction one blamed the estimator; direction two blamed the outcome-selected graded slice. Both are refuted by measurement: 100 of 101 multi-snapshot accounts move off their first hazard, and at each account's EARLIEST snapshot the hazard is 0.05 for 154 of 154 -- the whole book, not a selected 33. The cause is the coupler's own belief-selection rule. Landed as `4b6e1b29f` with the consequences taken: the `gap = 2.529` is not published in its current form, the re-run was not run because it could not have changed the answer, and no level move was available. Item three is the repair.

The noise-floor measurement now in flight patches a function the churn decision no longer calls, so it cannot see the thing it exists to measure. Observed, from the code and the process table: `simulation/customer_events.py:313-315` imports and calls `simulation.population_draw.price_elasticity_for_customer`; that function (line 1055) calls `_draw_curriculum_axis` directly and never routes through `price_sensitivity_for_customer` (line 997, still present); and `noise_floor.py:40` reassigns `pdraw.price_sensitivity_for_customer`. The rename landed in the working tree at 16:43-16:47Z and the two measurement processes started at 16:53:25Z, about nine minutes later. Its own docstring asserts that "patching the module attribute reaches the live decision", which was true when it was written and false when it was run. The predicted symptom is two seeds returning identical nets, which would read as a tight noise floor and is instead the signature of a dead knob -- the catalogued lesson that bit-for-bit reproduction across a world change is blindness, not stability. Caught before publication, not after.

The three-arm A/B run was killed 4m28s after launch and was still being described as in flight 2h12m later, by the parked Lane 0 file and by every reader after it. Observed: `docs/observability/three_arm_s1_run.log` carries its START line at 15:08:25Z, 56,229 lines, a last write at 15:12:53Z, no `END rc=` line and no traceback; `value_cycle_ab_s1_three_arm.json` does not exist; PID 1128717 is gone. The handoff document described this exact failure mode and told the next reader to check the log first; nobody did. Worth stating plainly that the alarm machinery was NOT at fault -- the finding fired and is on disk untracked.

Two consecutive directions, including mine, asserted that the company's CLV "cannot tell its accounts apart" and that 33 of 33 accounts recovering exactly 0.05 is "a FLOOR, not a belief", treating it as a property of the estimator. The constant hazard is a property of the graded slice. The conclusion was inferred from one component block and stated as established without reading the adjacent one, which is the R9 line. Item three carries the written correction.

Don't leave it claiming discoverable and don't wait for me to say so."* The instruction was right when written and wrong within two hours, and the tree already carries the edit. what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
